Module 1.title: Statics of Particles and Rigid Bodies (Coplanar Systems & Lami's Theorem)
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Statics & Equilibrium
  • Lami's Theorem: For three coplanar concurrent forces in equilibrium: $\frac{P}{\sin \alpha} = \frac{Q}{\sin \beta} = \frac{R}{\sin \gamma}$.
  • Equilibrium Equations: $\sum F_x = 0$, $\sum F_y = 0$, $\sum M_O = 0$.
  • Varignon's Theorem: The moment of a force about any point equals the algebraic sum of the moments of its components about the same point: $M_O = \sum (x F_y - y F_x)$.
  • Friction Laws (Coulomb): Limiting friction $F_{max} = \mu_s N$. Angle of friction $\phi = \tan^{-1}(\mu_s)$. Angle of repose equals angle of friction.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Module 1 Reference: Statics

Free Body Diagrams (FBD): Essential step isolating body and replacing all physical contacts, supports, and constraints with equivalent reaction force vectors.
Module 1.textbook_html:
1.1 Fundamental Principles of Statics

Engineering Mechanics studies the effect of forces acting on rigid bodies. A body is in static equilibrium if its translational acceleration and angular acceleration are simultaneously zero.

Module 2.title: Centroid, Centre of Gravity and Moment of Inertia
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Centroid & MOI
  • Centroid of Composite Area: $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum A_i x_i}{\sum A_i}$, $\bar{y} = \frac{\sum A_i y_i}{\sum A_i}$.
  • Parallel Axis Theorem: $I_{xx} = I_G + A d^2$. Radius of gyration $k = \sqrt{I / A}$.
  • Standard Area MOI:
    • Rectangle ($b \times h$): $I_G = \frac{b h^3}{12}$, $I_{base} = \frac{b h^3}{3}$.
    • Triangle ($b \times h$): $I_G = \frac{b h^3}{36}$, $I_{base} = \frac{b h^3}{12}$.
    • Circle (diameter $D$): $I_G = \frac{\pi D^4}{64}$.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: Moment of Inertia

Perpendicular Axis Theorem (for laminar planes): $I_{zz} = I_{xx} + I_{yy}$. Polar moment of inertia $J = I_{zz}$.
Module 2.textbook_html:
2.1 First and Second Moments of Area

The second moment of area (area moment of inertia $I$) reflects an area's resistance to bending deformation when configured into structural beams (I-beams, channels, angles).

Module 3.title: Analysis of Simple Trusses (Method of Joints & Sections)
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Trusses
  • Truss Determinacy: $m = 2j - 3$ (perfect/determinate). If $m < 2j - 3$ (deficient), if $m > 2j - 3$ (redundant).
  • Method of Joints: Isolate each joint where no more than 2 unknown forces exist. Apply $\sum F_x = 0, \sum F_y = 0$.
  • Method of Sections: Cut through no more than 3 members with unknown forces. Apply full rigid equilibrium $\sum F_x = 0, \sum F_y = 0, \sum M = 0$.
  • Zero-Force Member Rules:
    • Two non-collinear members meeting at an unloaded joint are both zero-force.
    • Three members meeting at an unloaded joint where two are collinear: the third member is zero-force.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Trusses

Truss assumptions: Members connected by frictionless pins; loads applied only at joints; member self-weight negligible; all members undergo axial tension or compression only.
Module 3.textbook_html:
3.1 Structural Truss Analysis Techniques

Trusses are planar or spatial structural frameworks composed of straight two-force members connected at pin joints. They provide exceptional load-carrying capacity with minimal material weight for bridges, roof trusses, and aerospace fuselages.

Module 4.title: Dynamics of Particles (Kinematics & Newton's Second Law)
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Particle Dynamics
  • Rectilinear Motion: $v = u + at$, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.
  • D'Alembert's Principle: $\sum \vec{F} - m\vec{a} = 0$. Treats dynamic acceleration as an equivalent static inertia force ($-m\vec{a}$).
  • Work-Energy Theorem: $U_{1-2} = \Delta KE = \frac{1}{2}m(v_2^2 - v_1^2)$.
  • Impulse-Momentum Principle: $\int_{t_1}^{t_2} \vec{F} dt = m\vec{v}_2 - m\vec{v}_1$.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Module 4 Reference: Dynamics

Curvilinear motion: Normal acceleration $a_n = v^2 / \rho$ directed toward center of curvature; Tangential acceleration $a_t = dv / dt$.
Module 4.textbook_html:
4.1 Kinematics and Kinetics of Particles

Newton's second law ($ ec{F} = d(m ec{v})/dt$) governs the accelerated motion of particles subjected to unbalanced resultant forces.

Module 5.title: Rigid Body Dynamics, Rotation and Simple Mechanical Vibrations
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Rotation & Vibrations
  • Fixed Axis Rotation: Torque $T = I_G \alpha$. Kinetic energy $KE = \frac{1}{2} I_G \omega^2$. General plane motion: $KE = \frac{1}{2} m v_G^2 + \frac{1}{2} I_G \omega^2$.
  • Instantaneous Centre of Zero Velocity (IC): Velocity of any point $P$ is $v_P = \omega \cdot r_{IC-P}$.
  • Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM): Equation $\ddot{x} + \omega_n^2 x = 0$. Natural frequency $\omega_n = \sqrt{k / m}$ (rad/s), $f_n = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{k/m}$ (Hz). Period $T = 2\pi / \omega_n$.
  • Simple Pendulum: $\omega_n = \sqrt{g / L}$. Compound pendulum: $\omega_n = \sqrt{\frac{m g h}{I_O}}$.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Module 5 Reference: Vibrations

Single degree of freedom undamped mass-spring systems undergo sinusoidal oscillations about their static equilibrium position.
Module 5.textbook_html:
5.1 Rotation and Undamped Mechanical Vibrations

Rigid body motion combines translation of the center of mass with rotation about that center. Mechanical vibrations arise from the dynamic exchange between kinetic energy and elastic potential strain energy.
